row.notes: MoverCollision resource factory (vtable slot 0x145a8f4e0: slot +0x60 of the vtable 0x145a8f480 installed at 0x1444583fa; the string 'MoverCollision' 0x145a8f01a lies 0x4c6 bytes before it): container must be JPAK (entries 0x20, count +8, table +0x20) or legacy BIGF (entries 0x18, trace 'very large alignment for a loaded bigfile'); creates one collision object per entry (0x1440caa60). For object version >0x20003, entry names NOT starting with 'qt_' or 'qt.' that contain lower-case 'sign' (case-sensitive: only the literal is lowered before the strstr) set, on the sub-object [obj+0x18] and only when its byte +0x164 is not already 0x18, collision type byte +0x164 = 0x18 (24) and the material +0x168 from +0xe8->+0x30->+0x1080; this is why 'qtsign.vcqtc' is a sign-collision tile. Track modding: tile naming rules for the TRN~ JPAK. | 2026-11-17 engine-re (track runtime round, static): JPAK entry = {name_off +0, size +4, data_off +8} (0x20 bytes, count +8, table +0x20). Entries are processed strictly in file order, one Ne_MoverCollision_BuildMoverShapes call each (0x144453b6b); the entry name is read only for the sign test (Ne_Crt_Strncmp 'qt_' / 'qt.' at 0x144453bcb / 0x144453be8, then Ne_Crt_Strstr with lower-case 'sign' at 0x144453c35). No sort, no quadtree parse, no ancestor check: tile names and their JPAK order carry no meaning for this loader. The qt_/qt./sign test runs only for tile version > 0x20003. When BuildMoverShapes returns 0 (only when its object pool is full, its error 0xc) this function records error 0xe in the error ring (0x144453dd0, 0x144453e6a), leaves the loop and returns the resource with only the tiles created so far (no crash on this path; later tiles silently missing; the query-context call is skipped then). With >= 0x261b (9755) entries and no failure it also calls Ne_MoverCollision_BuildQueryContext (cmp at 0x144453e92).
